A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCSC research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and extensions.

before.justification: V1 reports original checkpoint-merging experiments, generation-quality measurements, training-speed comparisons, and ablations on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds LSUN, LoRA, text-to-image, generalization, and search-behavior experiments.

M1.justification: The evolutionary search, FID objective, and affine checkpoint-combination framework remain. V3 replaces explicit coefficient normalization with searching differences from the first checkpoint, enforcing the sum constraint through its residual coefficient (Section 4.2; Algorithm 1). It also supports merging LoRA matrix-product updates. These are procedural refinements and extensions rather than a replacement method.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates image generation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64. V3 retains these datasets and adds LSUN-Cat and LSUN-Bedroom, plus text-conditioned generation trained/searched on CC12M and evaluated on MS-COCO (Sections 5.4–5.5; Appendix E.8). This substantially broadens both represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: The original EMA and EMA* comparisons remain. V3 adds unmerged LoRA fine-tuning controls in Table 5, vanilla LCM-LoRA training in Table 6, and released SDv1-5 and LoRA tuning in Table 19. These expand the controls for the new applications without substantially changing the original comparator set.

E3.justification: V3 adds test-set FID/KID evaluation and text-to-image protocols using 1K CC12M search pairs and 10K MS-COCO evaluation samples, preference metrics, and four-step-search/two-step-evaluation transfer. FCD is the existing FID@CLIP metric renamed. Some stated settings also change: the CIFAR-10 CT fine-tuning row reports batch size 512 instead of 128 in Table 1, without establishing whether this reflects rerunning or correction.

E4.justification: The original hyperparameter and convex-hull ablations are retained. V3 adds direct-versus-difference search comparisons (Tables 15–16), coefficient-magnitude/FID analysis, averaging across search seeds, coefficient-clipping experiments, search-pattern evolution, and convergence curves (Appendix F). Held-out and cross-dataset evaluations also directly examine generalization beyond the search objective and data.

E5.justification: V1 already compares two search seeds in Table 13; v3 retains their FIDs in Figure 11. V3 additionally specifies averaging coefficients from three and five different seeds in Figure 12. This adds seed-count information for a separate analysis, not evidence of increased repetition of the main benchmarks. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Many v1 scores survive as LCSC-Direct in v3 Tables 15–16, alongside new LCSC-Diff outcomes: CIFAR-10 CD at 800K has FID 2.44 versus Direct's 2.42, while ImageNet CD at 600+20K has 5.07 versus 5.54. These compare different search formulations. V3 also adds extensive LSUN, LoRA, text-to-image, and test-set results, while removing the original DM FID@CLIP result rows.

T1.justification: V1 provides background mathematics and empirical motivation without corresponding convergence proofs. V3 introduces a strongly convex SGD analysis, bounded gradient-second-moment assumptions, an EMA convergence bound with a residual term, and a theorem about mixtures of EMA checkpoints not being representable by a single EMA rate under linear independence. Appendix A supplies the new derivations and proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about reducing training cost and enhancing pretrained models remain, including the headline 23×/15× training speedups and 15-to-9 NFE reduction. V3 adds an explicit abstract/introduction claim of improved large text-to-image generation and presents theoretical analysis as an additional contribution. EMA suboptimality itself was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V1 interprets sparse, large coefficients as suggesting a lower-rank basin. V3 qualifies this interpretation: smaller, more homogeneous coefficients can also work, and search solutions may be connected through low-loss paths (Section 6; Appendix F). It adds explanations concerning search-pattern formation, harmful coefficient restrictions, EMA-rate dependence, and generalization across metrics and data. The existing future-work limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds implementation information for the new applications, including the Stable Diffusion v1-5 base, Dreamshaper-7 adapter insertion, checkpoint-saving windows and intervals, and baseline LoRA scale 0.15. Most original hardware and implementation disclosures remain. However, v1's project-code link and explicit CLIP ViT-B/32 specification are omitted; this establishes lost documentation, not that the code became unavailable.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning beyond empirical checkpoint averaging. Section 3 relates its analysis to SGD convergence work by Rakhlin, Shamir and Zhang, and Harvey; Appendix F connects search solutions to Garipov's mode-connectivity work. New LoRA, diffusion-training, preference-metric, and quantization references support the expanded scope. The original distinction from merging independently fine-tuned models remains.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the narrative. It condenses the main background while retaining extended material in Appendix B, moves Algorithm 1 and the hyperparameter study into appendices, separates the two experimental use cases, adds dedicated application/generalization subsections, and merges discussion with conclusion. These changes go beyond inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: V3 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially restructures tables and figure placement. It adds paired text-to-image examples, search-diagnostic plots, and new benchmark and ablation tables. Existing landscapes and generated-image grids are retained and relocated; the new grid heatmaps redisplay landscape measurements rather than establish a separate experiment.

improvement.justification: V3's test-set FID/KID and CC12M-to-MS-COCO evaluations substantially address v1's limited evidence about generalization beyond search data. LoRA, LSUN, and Stable Diffusion experiments broaden practical validation, while new ablations clarify search behavior and qualify the earlier coefficient interpretation. These evidential gains outweigh the omitted project-code link and some inconsistent iteration labels across tables. The improvement rests on stronger validation and explanation, not uniformly better reported scores.
